title: Length-prefixed stdout frame can grow result buffer without bounds
reasoning: processDetectionResults trusts the 32-bit length prefix from the Python child and keeps buffering until 4 + length bytes arrive. A faulty or compromised wakeword service can send a very large length and then stream arbitrary data or stop, causing the Electron main process to retain an ever-growing resultBuffer with no maximum frame size, reset, or process error. Because this runs in the main process, it can degrade or crash the desktop app.
recommendation: Define a maximum wakeword result frame size appropriate for the JSON messages, reject frames above that size, clear the buffer, emit/log an error, and consider stopping the child process when the framing protocol is violated.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for malformed stdout framing, oversized result frames, or buffer reset behavior after protocol violations.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a processDetectionResults-focused test that sends a length prefix above the configured maximum and verifies the buffer is cleared, no detection is emitted, and an error path is taken.
minimumFixScope: Add frame-size validation in processDetectionResults and cover malformed length-prefixed stdout input.
